A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey. Their complete text, tables, figures, and mathematical content support comparison across the extensive reorganization. v1 has no appendix; v2 includes Appendix A.

before.justification: v1 summarizes methods and outcomes attributed to cited studies. Its comparison table does not report an original empirical evaluation.

after.justification: v2 remains a literature survey. Table 1 explicitly derives generation-time information from surveyed papers, and Appendix A supplies metric formulas rather than original empirical results.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes a generative algorithm. v2 expands descriptions of published methods and adds model-selection guidance, without introducing or modifying a proposed model.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts training or evaluation on datasets. WiDS remains an illustrative example; additional application examples and reviewed methods do not establish new experimental task coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates a proposed method against baselines. Additions and removals in the surveyed model roster change literature coverage, not an experimentally evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: The surveyed evaluation framework expands substantially: v2 adds epistemic parity, alpha-precision, density and clipped density, a diversity evaluation section covering recall and coverage variants, and privacy evaluation using TPR at low FPR. These are additions to evaluation guidance in Section 3, not evidence of newly executed experiments.

E4.justification: Neither PDF reports original ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity analyses, or empirical case studies. The new requirement-relationship discussion is conceptual interpretation rather than supplementary experimental analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports study-level repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The seed-indexed epistemic-parity formula in Appendix A describes a metric, not runs performed or uncertainty estimated by this work.

E6.justification: v2 adds literature-attributed findings, including TabuLa's shorter training time than GReaT in Section 4.3 and tree-based diffusion's better fidelity and diversity than TabDDPM on small datasets in Section 4.7. These are additional reported findings, not new measurements or same-setting improvements over v1 experiments.

T1.justification: Most Appendix A equations simply explain established metrics. However, the new NNDR formula in Equation (27) is not equivalent to v1's verbal definition: its denominator measures a real-to-real distance instead of the synthetic record's distance to its second-closest real neighbor. This is a limited mathematical-definition discrepancy; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central taxonomy expands from four requirements to five through the addition of diversity. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion also newly emphasize relationships among requirements and a practical selection roadmap, substantially broadening the survey's stated contribution.

C2.justification: New Section 3.6 explains reinforcement and tension among requirements, including alignment versus fidelity when real data contain errors. v2 also discusses misleading privacy metrics, non-deep-learning alternatives, and clarifies that model classifications indicate research focus rather than exclusive capabilities.

D1.justification: Table 1 newly explains that timing categories aggregate published generation times for 10,000 samples: fast below 0.5 seconds, medium above 0.5 and below 1 second, and slow otherwise. v1 only describes relative speed. This documents the compilation procedure without establishing reruns; no code or data release is added.

R1.justification: v2 adds substantial coverage of foundation models, private neural generators, non-deep-learning alternatives, and evaluation literature. Table 1 adds GEM, GEM+, DP-MERF, DP-NTK, TabuLa, TabTransGAN, and TabPFN, while removing TabGFN. Section 5 expands comparisons with other surveys and sharpens the user-oriented positioning.

P1.justification: v1 interleaves evaluation and methods within requirement-specific Sections 3–6. v2 separates requirements and metrics into Section 3 and reorganizes retained method descriptions by architecture in Section 4. The introduction and discussion expand substantially, with new broader-impact text and Appendix A.

P2.justification: v2 adds the selection roadmap in Figure 1 and metric-summary Table 2, restructures Table 1 chronologically with a diversity column, and redraws the requirement diagram with five categories. The retained architecture schematic is rearranged, and the document switches from two-column to single-column layout.

improvement.justification: v2 provides better guidance through diversity coverage, statistical utility, explicit requirement trade-offs, and the selection roadmap. These address substantive gaps in v1. The gain is tempered by new technical inconsistencies: Appendix A's density Equation (18) does not implement the neighborhood-counting description in Section 3.3, and NNDR Equation (27) conflicts with the retained prose definition. These errors limit the reliability of the expanded reference material.
